It started on August 2, 2013 and ended on May 24, 2014. Twenty teams competed in the league, seventeen returning from the 2012–13 season and three promoted from the Primera B Nacional Championship (Championship winners [[Rosario Central]], runners-up [[Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia y Esgrima (LP)]] and 3rd place [[Club Olimpo|Olimpo]]). For first time [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] did not compete in the Primera División championship. In the first half of the season [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] became champion of the 2013 Torneo Inicial "Nietos Recuperados", winning the “Miguel Benancio Sánchez” League Cup. The winner of the 2014 Torneo Final "Nietos Recuperados", [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]], won the "Presidente Raúl Alfonsín" League Cup. In the Superfinal, River Plate won the Campeonato Cup after a 1–0 victory over San Lorenzo in La Punta, San Luis. [[Argentinos Juniors]] and [[All Boys]] were relegated to the Primera B Nacional Championship. The third relegated team was [[Club Atlético Colón|Colón]], who lost a playoff match against [[Atlético de Rafaela]]. ==Format== There was two champions in the season. The champions (Torneo Inicial and Torneo Final winners) met in a season ending championship final to determine the super champion. The format for each tournament remained the same as in previous seasons. As in the previous season the last three teams on the relegation (average) table were directly relegated. ==Teams== The relegated teams of 2012–13 season were [[San Martín de San Juan|San Martín (SJ)]], [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] and [[Unión de Santa Fe|Unión]]. They played in the 2013–14 Primera B Nacional Championship. At the same time the 2012–13 Primera B Nacional Championship winners [[Rosario Central]], runners-up [[Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia y Esgrima (LP)]] and 3rd place [[Club Olimpo|Olimpo]] were promoted at the end of the season. ===Stadia and locations=== {{location map+ |Argentina |float=right |width=325 |caption=Locations of the 2013−14 Primera División teams outside [[Greater Buenos Aires]]. |places= {{location map~ |Argentina |lat=-34.603611 |long=-58.381667 |label=

It began on August 2 and ended on December 15, 2013. Originally the tournament should finish on December 8, but [[Argentine Football Association|AFA]] decided to postpone two matches of the last round (Vélez Sarsfield-San Lorenzo and Newell's Old Boys-Lanús) one week as [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]] had to play the [[2013 Copa Sudamericana]] final against Ponte Preta of Brazil. [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] won the title with a 0–0 draw at Vélez Sarsfield as outgoing champions Newell's Old Boys were held 2–2 in Rosario. San Lorenzo topped the Torneo Inicial with 33 points from 19 matches, two more than Vélez Sarsfield, Newell's Old Boys and Lanús. It was San Lorenzo's 12th league title in the professional era and first since the 2007 Clausura championship.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-san-lorenzo-clinch-argentine-title-004009859--sow.html |title=San Lorenzo clinch Argentine title |date=December 15, 2013 |work=Yahoo}}{{cite web |url=http://canchallena.lanacion.com.ar/1647967-en-vivo-san-lorenzo-velez-torneo-inicial-fecha-19-definicion |title=Torneo Inicial: San Lorenzo es el nuevo campeón del fútbol argentino |date=December 15, 2013 |work=Canchallena |language=es |access-date=December 16, 2013 |archive-date=December 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222130051/http://canchallena.lanacion.com.ar/1647967-en-vivo-san-lorenzo-velez-torneo-inicial-fecha-19-definicion |url-status=dead }}

Atlante|Atlante]] over [[Juan Carlos Falcón]] back in 2007. Atlante decided to take this issue to [[FIFA]] and they won the case. Tigre]] || 10 || 6,400 |- | style{{=}}"text-align:center;"| _row_count || [[Arsenal de Sarandí]] || 10 || 2,160 |- |} }} ==Torneo Final== The '''Torneo Final''' was the second and final tournament of the season. It began on February 7 and ended on May 19, 2014. [[Club Atlético Colón|Colón]] was leader of the Torneo Final until the 11th round, then [[Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes (LP)]], [[Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia y Esgrima (LP)]] and [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] started to fight for the lead of the tournament until the last round. In the last round [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] trashed [[Quilmes Atlético Club|Quilmes]] 5-0 as [[Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes (LP)]] and [[Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia y Esgrima (LP)]] were beaten 2–1 by [[Club Atlético Tigre|Tigre]] and 0–1 by [[Boca Juniors]] respectively. Finally River Plate won the Torneo Final with a five-point margin over Boca Juniors, Estudiantes (LP) and Godoy Cruz in joint second place.{{cite web|url=http://www.buenosairesherald.com/article/159832/sweet-dreams|title=Sweet dreams |date=May 19, 2014|work=Buenos Aires Herald}}{{cite web|url=http://canchallena.lanacion.com.ar/1692479-river-quilmes-torneo-final-2014-monumental-ramon-diaz |title=River es campeón del fútbol argentino después de seis años y vivió una fiesta en Núñez |date=May 18, 2014|work=Canchallena|language=es}} One of the fundamental moments in the title of River Plate was the victory 1–2 to Boca Juniors in the 10th round with a head goal of [[Ramiro Funes Mori]] in the last minutes of the match. This was their first away victory over Boca Juniors in 10 years.{{cite web|url=http://www.buenosairesherald.com/article/155803/funes-mori-supercl%C3%A1sico-hero-for-victorious-river|title=Funes Mori Superclásico hero for victorious River |date=March 30, 2014|work=Buenos Aires Herald}}{{cite web|url=http://canchallena.lanacion.com.ar/1676695-boca-river-en-vivo-superclasico-torneo-final-2014 |title=River le ganó a Boca 2-1 sobre el final y es escolta en el torneo |date=March 30, 2014|work=Canchallena|language=es}}
With [[Argentinos Juniors]] and [[All Boys]] relegated previously, the third relegation place had a dramatic final in the last round after [[Club Atlético Colón|Colón]] and [[Atlético de Rafaela]] scored injury-time winners to win their games, at home to Olimpo and away to Arsenal respectively, forcing a play-off match between them.{{cite web|url=http://www.buenosairesherald.com/article/159764/heartstopping-finish-leaves-relegation-playoff-for-col%C3%B3n-rafaela |title=Heart-stopping finish leaves relegation play-off for Colón, Rafaela |date=May 18, 2014|work=Buenos Aires Herald}}
